exposure: Maternal age less than 20 years at delivery
outcome: Gynaecological complications (post-partum haemorrhage, low birth weight, perineal tears)
Adverse social determinants of health (smoking, mental illness, low breastfeeding rates)
cohort: The study included 473 pregnant women aged 13-19 years (median 18) who delivered at a tertiary hospital in Stoke-on-Trent, UK, between January 2020 and December 2022.
finding: Pregnant women under 20 in socially deprived areas of the UK were more likely to experience negative gynaecological and social outcomes, such as higher rates of post-partum haemorrhage and low birth weight, compared to national averages and less deprived areas.
mod_finding: The induction rate (28.2%) and caesarean section rate (18.4%) among the cohort were below national averages, with 43% undergoing spontaneous delivery.
